1-5-2.title: Functionalism
1-5-2.explanation: Functionalism shifted attention from analysing the contents of consciousness to the functions of mental activity and behaviour. William James is the central association. The approach asks how mind and behaviour help people function, adapt and respond to their surroundings. A key exam distinction is Functionalism is not the search for the elements of consciousness. That emphasis belongs to structuralism. James was interested in how consciousness operates in real life and in adaptation. For exam application, If a PYQ asks which school is concerned with how the mind helps a person adapt, think William James and functionalism as the first retrieval cue. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are functions of mind, everyday functioning.

1-5-3.title: Psychoanalytical psychology
1-5-3.explanation: Psychoanalytical psychology, as presented in the supplied sources, centres on unconscious processes, conflict and the influence of repressed wishes and experiences on behaviour. Freud's model includes id, ego and superego; psychoanalysis aims to bring repressed unconscious material into consciousness and develop insight. A key exam distinction is Do not confuse repression with rationalization. Repression removes threatening material from conscious awareness, whereas rationalization supplies a rational-sounding explanation for a failure or transgression. For exam application, If a stem describes symptoms as indirect expressions of repressed wishes or asks about bringing unconscious material into consciousness, retrieve the psychoanalytic framework. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are id, ego, superego, pleasure principle.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Do not reduce psychoanalysis to one motive.

1-5-4.title: Gestalt psychology
1-5-4.explanation: Gestalt psychology argues that psychological experience, especially perception, cannot always be understood by simply adding isolated sensory elements. The organised pattern or whole matters. Wertheimer, Koffka and Köhler are central figures. A key exam distinction is The key contrast is whole versus isolated elements. Structuralism analyses elements; Gestalt psychology emphasizes the organisation and pattern in which those elements are experienced. For exam application, When a question describes a melody, visual pattern or apparent movement whose experience depends on the relationship among parts, identify the Gestalt principle rather than an element-by-element analysis. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are organized whole, pattern/configuration, insight learning.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Gestalt is broader than insight learning.

1-5-6.title: Humanistic-Existential psychology
1-5-6.explanation: The supplied NET framework treats Humanistic-Existential psychology as a major reaction against narrow accounts of people. Its emphasis is on subjective experience, meaning, agency, personal growth and the individual's relationship with existence rather than reducing behaviour to only observable responses or unconscious drives. A key exam distinction is The key contrast is emphasis: behaviorism foregrounds observable behaviour; psychoanalysis foregrounds unconscious conflict; humanistic-existential approaches foreground lived experience, agency, meaning and growth. For exam application, When a question highlights authenticity, personal meaning, choice, self-development or lived experience, retrieve the humanistic-existential orientation. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are existential choice, reaction against reductionism.

The psychological emphasis is on experiences and states that extend beyond ordinary personal identity and on their possible relation to consciousness and self-development. For exam application, When a stem focuses on transcending ordinary identity or studying expanded states of consciousness, retrieve the transpersonal orientation. The exam-relevant terms and relationships to retain are expanded consciousness, transcendence, altered states.
